name: Frame
simple: A Frame is a plain rectangle. It's the most basic UI building block: use it as a colored box, a background panel, or a container that holds other UI like buttons and text. Health bars, menu windows and pop-ups usually start as a Frame.
analogy: A Frame is like a piece of cardboard. You can paint it, cut it to any size, and glue other things (labels, buttons, pictures) onto it.
whenToUse: A background panel behind a menu
A container that groups buttons and text so you can move or hide them together
A simple colored bar, like the filling of a health bar
A box to hold a UIListLayout or UIGridLayout
where: Inside a ScreenGui (on screen), SurfaceGui (on a part) or BillboardGui (floating). Create it in Studio under StarterGui or with Instance.new("Frame") in a LocalScript.

terms.UI / GUI: User Interface: the buttons, menus, text and pictures drawn on the screen or on things in the game.
terms.LocalScript: A script that runs on the player's own device. All UI code goes in LocalScripts.
terms.ScreenGui: The invisible container that holds UI shown on the player's screen. It must be inside the player's PlayerGui (put it in StarterGui in Studio).
terms.parent: The object something is placed inside.
terms.UDim2: The value used for Size and Position: (X Scale, X Offset, Y Scale, Y Offset). Scale is a fraction (0 to 1) of the parent's size; Offset is exact pixels.
terms.pixel: One tiny dot on the screen.
terms.transparency: How see-through something is. 0 = solid, 1 = invisible.
terms.Color3: A color made of red, green and blue amounts, like Color3.fromRGB(255, 0, 0) for red.
terms.container: Something that holds other things. Moving or hiding a container moves or hides everything in it.
terms.Scale: A fraction of the parent's size. Size X Scale 0.5 = half the parent's width.
terms.Offset: Exact pixels that don't change with screen size.

examples.title: A health bar that shrinks when you get hurt
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")

local screenGui = Instance.new("ScreenGui")
screenGui.Name = "HealthGui"
screenGui.Parent = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")

-- The dark background of the bar
local back = Instance.new("Frame")
back.Size = UDim2.fromOffset(300, 30)
back.AnchorPoint = Vector2.new(0.5, 1)
back.Position = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 1, -20) -- bottom middle, 20 px up from the bottom
back.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(40, 40, 40)
back.Parent = screenGui

-- The green filling, sized as a fraction of the background
local fill = Instance.new("Frame")
fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(1, 1) -- start full
fill.BackgroundColor3 = Color3.fromRGB(60, 200, 80)
fill.BorderSizePixel = 0
fill.Parent = back

local function update()
	local percent = humanoid.Health / humanoid.MaxHealth -- a number from 0 to 1
	fill.Size = UDim2.fromScale(percent, 1)
end

humanoid.HealthChanged:Connect(update)
update()
explain: StarterCharacterScripts puts this LocalScript inside your character, so script.Parent is the character.
back is a 300x30 pixel dark bar at the bottom middle of the screen.
fill is INSIDE back, so its Scale is measured against back. Scale 1 = 300 pixels wide, Scale 0.5 = 150 pixels.
Health / MaxHealth gives a number from 0 to 1. At 50 of 100 health, percent = 0.5, so the green part is half the bar.
HealthChanged runs update every time health changes.

gotchas: Children's Scale sizes are a fraction of the Frame, not the screen.
To hide only the box but keep its children, use BackgroundTransparency = 1. To hide everything, use Visible = false.
Children can spill outside the frame. Turn on ClipsDescendants to cut them off.

Frame.Style.simple: Picks one of Roblox's old built-in looks for the frame (like a dark rounded box). The default, Custom, lets you style it yourself with BackgroundColor3 and friends, which is what most games do.
Frame.Style.example:
local frame = script.Parent
frame.Style = Enum.FrameStyle.Custom -- style it yourself
